summary: Astrid Zotter is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Leipzig. She held postdoctoral and editorial roles at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and Documenta Nepalica in 2018, and was affiliated with the University of Heidelberg in 2023.

Atsuhiko Yoshida (1934–2024) was a religious studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Seikei University, University of Tokyo, University of Strasbourg, Athénée Français, and École Pratique des Hautes Études under mentor Georges Dumézil. He held posts at CNRS, Seikei University, and Gakushuin University.
Atsushi Ibuki (b. 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. He was attested as a professor at Toyo University in 2015.

Atsushi Kanazawa (b. 1951) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held teaching positions at Meteorological College and Komazawa University, where he served as lecturer and associate professor between 1987 and 2012.

Atsushi Kiyozawa (b. 1951) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Delhi and held a lecturer post at Kindai University, attested in 1989.

Atsushi Uno (b. 1922) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University, Banaras Hindu University, and under T. R. V. Murti, Raghunath Giri, and other teachers. He held academic posts at Shuchiin, Kyoto, Tokai, Hiroshima, and Kindai universities.

Atsuuji Ashikaga (1901–1983) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Doshisha University and Kyoto University under Ryosaburo Sakaki. He was a professor at Kyoto University and Tokai University, and president of the Society for Near Eastern Studies in Japan.
Atsuyoshi Keika (b. 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He held posts at Otani University as a lecturer (attested 1990) and professor (attested 2014).

Atul Chandra Chatterjee (1874–1955) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at the University of Calcutta, Presidency University under Charles Henry Tawney, and King's College, Cambridge. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1897 to 1931.

August Boeckh (1785–1867) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg under Friedrich August Wolf and Friedrich Schleiermacher, later serving as a professor at the University of Heidelberg (1807–1811) and the University of Berlin (1811–1861).

August Conrady (1864–1925) was a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Würzburg and University of Leipzig, later serving on the faculty at Leipzig from 1891 until his professorship, as well as at Peking University (1903–1904).

August Dillmann (1823–1894) was a linguistics and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held academic posts at the universities of Tübingen, Kiel, Giessen, and Berlin from approximately 1848 until his death in 1894.

August Fick (1833–1916) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He held a professorship in comparative linguistics at Göttingen starting in 1876 and served as an ordinary professor at the University of Breslau from 1888 to 1891.

August Fischer (1865–1949) was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held a post at the University of Leipzig from around 1900 to 1930 and served on the board of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

August Friedrich Pott (1802–1887) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Franz Bopp. After lecturing in Berlin, he served as professor of general linguistics at the University of Halle from 1833 and co-founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft in 1845.

August Hermann Francke (1870–1930) was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and history. He studied at the Niesky Lehrerseminar, Moravian Theological College, and the University of Berlin, where he served as a Privatdozent beginning in 1922.

August Hjalmar Edgren (1840–1903) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Uppsala, Cornell, and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held teaching posts at Yale, Lund University, University of Gothenburg as rector, and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

August Johan Bernet Kempers (1906–1992) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Leiden University. He directed the Pusat Penelitian Arkeologi Nasional (~1936–1956) and held positions at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and the University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien (1840–1916) was a linguist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Jena under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He taught at Göttingen and Jena, and was a professor at the University of Leipzig from 1870 to 1915.

August Schleicher (1821–1868) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, Erlangen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald and Friedrich Ritschl. He held academic posts at the University of Bonn, University of Prague, and University of Jena.
